description: DB integration: migrations create occurrences table with partial unique open-per-schedule index; backfill creates exactly one open occurrence per active schedule and none for inactive
DB integration: inserting a second open occurrence for the same schedule violates the unique index
listMaintenanceOccurrences returns only the caller's tenant and only authorized assets; filters (status, client, type, due range) and pagination behave
createOccurrenceTicket called twice returns the same ticket (no duplicate); creates asset_associations link and stamps occurrence.ticket_id; carries maintenance context into the ticket

completeOccurrence happy path: one history row, occurrence closed, next_maintenance advanced from completion date per cadence (monthly, quarterly, interval>1 cases), new open occurrence created — all in one transaction
completeOccurrence rejects: already-closed occurrence (double completion), schedule from another asset, another tenant, and unauthenticated/underprivileged user
Late completion advances from actual completion date, not the stored due date (documented rule)
'custom' frequency completion is rejected rather than treated as daily
skipOccurrence closes as skipped with reason, advances next due, opens next occurrence, writes no completion history
Pause cancels the open occurrence and removes the plan from actionable lists/aggregates; reactivate recreates one open occurrence
Editing next_maintenance on a schedule moves its open occurrence's due_date
Deleting a schedule with history archives instead of deleting; history and occurrences remain queryable; hard delete works when no history
getMaintenanceAggregates counts match a hand-built fixture (overdue/due today/upcoming), and compliance is on-time completions ÷ due occurrences — a plan with no history is not compliant
REST/mobile record endpoint still accepts the existing contract, routes through occurrence completion, and rejects a second completion of the same occurrence

UI smoke (dev stack): /msp/assets/maintenance renders real workspace; filter to overdue; create ticket from an occurrence; clicking again opens the same ticket; complete via drawer; history gains the record and next due advances — screenshot evidence
UI smoke: calendar view toggle shows the month grid, chips reflect occurrence statuses, clicking a chip opens the same detail pane, and completion from calendar view updates chips and KPIs
UI smoke: asset detail Maintenance tab completion works and paused plan disappears from workspace actionable view
